questions.question: Please provide a source for “first recorded by Diophantus” and “first appeared in Europe in Liber quadratorum (1225)”, and clarify which sum-of-two-squares result is attributed to Fermat in the introduction. The post gives no bibliographic locator for these historical claims; the arithmetic and both identity forms are preserved and checked separately.

localizations.ru: Подтвердить источником исторические формулировки «впервые опубликовано Диофантом» и «в Европе впервые появилось в Liber quadratorum (1225)», а также уточнить, какой именно результат о сумме двух квадратов приписан Ферма в вводном абзаце. questions.resolution: The priority claims were removed; the introduction now identifies Fermat’s theorem for primes of the form 4k+1.

questions.question: Provide exact bibliographic locators for the remaining historical claims: the book/problem in Diophantus’s Arithmetica, the passage in Brahmagupta’s Brahmasphutasiddhanta, and the section/problem in Fibonacci’s Liber quadratorum that contains this product-of-two-sums-of-squares identity. Removing priority wording does not by itself substantiate these attributions.

questions.resolution: Added exact locators for Diophantus (III.19), Brahmagupta (18.64–65) and Fibonacci (Proposition 6), with edition links and a distinction between a numerical case and the general composition rule.
